clue.text: Islands where whaler returned, by degrees

indicators.note: returned signals that the word for the whaler is read backwards

parts.note: Captain Ahab is the whale-hunter of Moby-Dick
MAs are Master of Arts degrees

explanation.surface: A whaling captain comes back to some islands, gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: Ahab is the obsessed captain in Melville's Moby-Dick; 'by degrees' looks like 'gradually' but supplies the academic qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names an Atlantic archipelago, a group of islands.

clue.text: Gang going over river for combined meal

indicators.note: going over means the gang word straddles the river letter

parts.note: a bunch is a group or gang

explanation.surface: A gang crosses a river on the way to a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-morning meal blends breakfast and lunch into one.

clue.text: Emperor specially hard on Scot?

indicators.note: specially here means the letters of hard are arranged in a special new order

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: An emperor who was particularly tough on the Scots.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the wall built to keep the Scots out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman ruler who built a wall across northern Britain was an emperor.

clue.text: Libertine breaking up demonstration in African city

indicators.note: breaking up means the libertine word splits the demonstration word

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration
a rake is a dissolute man

explanation.surface: A debauchee disrupts a protest in a North African city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan city is a major urban centre in North Africa.

clue.text: A lot of students formed a row, made more efficient

parts.note: a stream is a set of school pupils grouped by ability
lined means stood in a line

explanation.surface: Many pupils queued up, which was quicker.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a STREAM is a class grouping by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Simplified and reorganised to work better, like a sleek shape.

clue.text: Scientist I put in old ship not quite finished

indicators.note: put in means the letter I is placed inside the shortened ship word
not quite finished means the last letter of the ship's word is dropped

parts.note: a galleon was a large old sailing ship

explanation.surface: Someone shoves the narrator aboard an old vessel that was never completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite finished' cuts the final N from GALLEON to leave GALLEO; 'put in' inserts I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian astronomer who championed the heliocentric model is a famous scientist.

clue.text: Empty talk that's quickly stepped on

definitions.meaning: the accelerator pedal, pressed down for speed

explanation.surface: Idle chatter that is soon squashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle chatter is hot air, and the accelerator is a pedal one presses to go faster.

clue.text: Served in glass, iced or chilled drink

indicators.note: served in means the drink is contained within the words glass, iced

explanation.surface: A cold drink served in a glass with ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian yoghurt-based beverage is served cold.

clue.text: Corrupt stealer who was advised not to lend or borrow

definitions.text: who was advised not to lend or borrow

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters of stealer are perverted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crooked thief who was warned against lending and borrowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Polonius tells his son in Hamlet 'Neither a borrower nor a lender be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Polonius's son in Hamlet receives the famous advice against lending or borrowing.

clue.text: Expert helping people see work by Italian master, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken and match the sound of the entry

parts.note: op (opus, a work) followed by Titian, the Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A specialist helping people appreciate a painting by an Italian old master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' suggests appreciating art, but it means eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who tests eyes and fits glasses helps people see.

clue.text: Prepared for war in sensitive areas

definitions.meaning: troops mobilised and carrying weapons are ready for battle
the armpits are ticklish, sensitive parts of the body

explanation.surface: Someone armed for battle in delicate places.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-word phrase for soldiers carrying weapons, and as one word the armpits, often ticklish.

clue.text: It usually gets blanket coverage in a newspaper

definitions.meaning: the bed linen layer lies beneath the blanket
a paper, especially a tabloid, is informally called this

explanation.surface: A story covered by every outlet appears in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blanket coverage' suggests saturation reporting, but it means literally covered by a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed linen lies under a blanket, and a newspaper is informally a rag or paper of this name.

clue.text: Genial feature associated with a country out east

parts.note: genial in anatomy means relating to the chin, so the feature is the point of the jaw

explanation.surface: A friendly face is linked with a nation in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genial' reads as 'friendly', but in anatomy it means 'of the chin'.
explanation.definitionFit: The People's Republic is a large nation in East Asia.

clue.text: One caught after attending robbery is not religious

indicators.note: after places the one and caught letters behind the attending and robbery pieces

parts.note: attending means present at, giving AT
a heist is a robbery
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A robber is arrested having been at the scene, and has no faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone denying the existence of any god is by definition without religion.

clue.text: Possible result of arranging hearing — shot for this?

definitions.text: Possible result of arranging hearing — shot for this?

indicators.note: arranging tells us the letters of hearing and shot are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being arraigned may lead to execution by firing squad for this crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the crime: a hearing is arranged, and the traitor could be shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal of one's country was a capital crime for which a person might be shot.

clue.text: Elected to reveal one chap is back with a well-educated class

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
to tell is to reveal or disclose
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gent is a chap or man

indicators.note: back means the word is is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A man chosen to disclose that someone has returned with the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: The term refers to intellectuals collectively, a cultured, educated elite.

clue.text: Less sensitive individual is leader

parts.note: number here means more numb
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: The thick-skinned one is the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is 'more numb', not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The top person, the chief, is idiomatically first in rank.

clue.text: Criticism of reliable chap joining club

parts.note: a brick is a dependable, solid person in British slang
a bat is a club

explanation.surface: A dependable man is criticised on joining a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You're a brick' is old British praise for a dependable friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostile remark is figuratively a missile thrown at someone.

clue.text: Number involved with tough lad in free-for-all

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of the three words are tangled up together

explanation.surface: A gang of hard youths gets mixed up in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure, but its letters are simply anagram fodder with TOUGH LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy, disorderly scuffle with no rules is a free-for-all.

clue.text: Even a soldier must assume this

definitions.meaning: the regulation clothing put on by a serviceman

explanation.surface: Even a soldier has to accept this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb opening the sentence; it is the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Consistent throughout, and the regulation dress a serviceman puts on.

clue.text: Practical joke from member with influence

parts.note: a leg is a limb or member
pull means clout or influence

explanation.surface: A prank played by an MP with connections.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing someone with a tall story is a hoax, a joking deception.

clue.text: Run into brutal person in 11

indicators.note: into means the run letter goes inside the brutal person word

parts.note: a fiend is a cruel or brutal person
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Bumping into a thug somewhere in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 across is CHINA, Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china plate stands for mate, a pal.

clue.text: As ordered, I checked a flier from America

indicators.note: as ordered tells us the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone checks an aircraft from the US as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a pilot or plane, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small North American songbird of the tit family is a flier from America.

clue.text: Worked on computer as king watched

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A typist works while the monarch looks on.
explanation.definitionFit: Typing data in at a keyboard is inputting it.

clue.text: Earl's son and daughter, in a fashion, flipped

indicators.note: flipped means the whole assembled piece is turned round
in places the daughter's letter inside the word for fashion

parts.note: a rage is a craze or fashion, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: A nobleman's boy and girl turn over, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: D inside RAGE makes RADGE, which 'flipped' turns round. In King Lear the Earl of Gloucester has two sons, the legitimate one being the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's King Lear, Gloucester's legitimate heir bears this name, so he is an Earl's son.

clue.text: Sort of trap for marine bird

definitions.meaning: a hidden practical-joke or explosive trap set for the unwary
a tropical seabird related to the gannet

explanation.surface: A snare meant to catch a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: A disguised device sprung on the unwary is a trap of this kind, and a gannet-like seabird shares the name.

clue.text: Like a rake, mixing dust, soil, and earth, initially

indicators.note: mixing means the letters of dust and soil are stirred together
initially picks the first letter of earth

explanation.surface: A garden rake is used to blend dust, soil and earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like the garden tool, but it is a libertine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a debauched man, so a person like one leads a debauched, immoral life.

clue.text: Needing a drink — like some wine?

explanation.surface: Thirsty, like certain wines.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched means thirsty, and a wine without sweetness is described this way.

clue.text: Little boy without purpose and without courage

parts.note: Tim, short for Timothy, as in Tiny Tim of A Christmas Carol
idly means aimlessly, without purpose

explanation.surface: A young lad aimlessly lacking bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting fearfully and shyly is acting without bravery.

clue.text: Influenced by poverty, got angry

definitions.meaning: led by need, i.e. driven by want

explanation.surface: Someone driven by want became cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the answer as NEED-LED.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, driven by want; as one word, irritated or riled.
